definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(1/(r! in C)) x^r; composition is the endomorphism product, the zeroth power is the identity.

definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(1/(r! in C)) y^r.
U=V(K)=M⊗_Z K, the balanced tensor product of integer modules. Its K-action is a·(m⊗b)=m⊗(ab).

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C)
definitions.definition: U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra generated by the elements X_r and Y_r for all natural r, acting on V by the specified representation.

L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K, equipped, whenever the commutator relations and lattice stability in the original assumptions hold, with their induced commutator bracket and action on U. The bracket normalization is [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, including characteristic 2.

inputs.statement: V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. Its endomorphisms x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h. The vector v∈V is nonzero and satisfies xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary free abelian subgroup with an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and M is stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! (r∈N). The induced x,y,h actions on V(K)=M⊗_Z K are the actions in the target.

output.statement: For every natural number r, X_r(M)⊆M and Y_r(M)⊆M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M. The given endomorphism h=xy−yx also satisfies h(M)⊆M: for every m∈M, h(m)=x(y(m))−y(x(m)) belongs to M. Thus x,y,h and all X_r,Y_r restrict to Z-linear endomorphisms of M.

binders.type: element of the additive subgroup M

argument.text: For every natural r, X_r and Y_r belong to the subalgebra U_Z by its definition as the integer algebra generated by all these operators. H003 says M is stable under this algebra, so X_r(M)⊆M and Y_r(M)⊆M. In particular, since 1!=1, X_1=x and Y_1=y; thus x,y preserve M.

produces.statement: For every natural r, X_r and Y_r preserve M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M.

argument.text: H002 identifies the given endomorphism h with xy−yx. For every m∈M, F001 places x(y(m)) and y(x(m)) in M; since M is an additive subgroup, their difference is in M. Therefore h(M)⊆M. Every listed complex-linear map is additive and respects integer multiples; its restriction to M is consequently an integer-linear endomorphism. This proves the output statement without using any induced operator or assuming any further hypothesis.
